title: Roman to Integer
corePattern: Hash Table Lookup with Subtractive Pair Handling via Linear Scan
interviewTips: Ask if input is guaranteed to be a valid Roman numeral in range 1 to 3999 — this lets you assume only the 6 legal subtractive pairs (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM) appear.

Trade-off to discuss: explicit 13-entry map with 2-char lookahead vs 7-entry map with value comparison — both O(n) time O(1) space, but right-to-left max-tracking avoids substring creation and double lookup.
Edge-case tip: single character (e.g., I, M), all subtractive string (e.g., CMXCIX = 999), and longest valid input MMMCMXCIX = 3999; ensure i+1 bounds check and correct add vs subtract decision.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force with Explicit Subtractive Map
approaches.intuition: There are only 13 meaningful symbols: 7 singles (I,V,X,L,C,D,M) and 6 subtractive pairs (IV,IX,XL,XC,CD,CM). Scan left to right, and at each position greedily try to consume 2 characters if they form a known subtractive pair, otherwise consume 1 character.
approaches.theory: Roman numerals are normally additive, except when a smaller value precedes a larger value, which means subtraction. Instead of reasoning about ordering, enumerate all subtractive cases in a hash table. Left-to-right scan is correct because valid Roman numerals have a unique greedy tokenization: if s[i:i+2] is in the table it must be taken as one token (e.g., CM=900 not C+M=1100). Each index advances by 1 or 2, so each character is visited once.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single left-to-right pass over n characters, each step does O(1) hash lookup. Substring of length 2 is O(1). Total O(n) where n = len(s) <= 15.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Hash table holds fixed 13 entries independent of input size, plus a few integer variables.

steps: i=0: s[0:2]='MC' not in map -> add M=1000, total=1000, i=1
i=1: s[1:3]='CM' in map -> add 900, total=1900, i=3
i=3: s[3:5]='XC' in map -> add 90, total=1990, i=5
i=5: s[5:7]='IV' in map -> add 4, total=1994, i=7

edgeCases: Single char: 'I' -> 1, 'M' -> 1000, no pair lookup needed

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Right-to-Left Single Pass
approaches.intuition: Scan from right to left keeping the maximum value seen so far. If current value >= max-so-far, it is additive; if current value < max-so-far, it must be a subtractive prefix and should be subtracted. This needs only the 7 single symbols.
approaches.theory: In a valid Roman numeral, values generally decrease left-to-right except for subtractive prefixes which are smaller than the following larger symbol. When scanning right-to-left, prev tracks the largest value to the right. Invariant: prev = max of all processed suffix values. If cur < prev, cur is a subtractive prefix of a larger numeral to its right, so subtract it; otherwise add it and update prev = cur. This correctly handles IV=5-1, IX, XL, etc., without explicitly enumerating pairs and without lookahead or substring allocation.

timeComplexity.explanation: One reverse pass over n characters with O(1) array/hash lookup per character.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only 7-entry map (or fixed array of size 128/256) plus total and prev variables.

edgeCases: LVIII -> 58: all cur >= prev, pure addition
IX -> 9, XL -> 40, CM -> 900: same subtract logic
